text: {"domains":{"block_M":[32,64,128],"block_N":[64,128],"block_K":[32,64],"num_stages":[1,2,3],"threads":[128],"swizzle":[0,4,8,16]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1,"launches":1,"pipeline":1.5,"footprint":0.75},"rationale":"Two observations so far. Attempt-00 (block_M=128, block_N=64, block_K=64, num_stages=1, swizzle=0) passed numerical, compiled, and simulated at 470.78 us with 32768 actual smem (exactly at the portability cap). Attempt-01 (block_M=64, block_N=128, block_K=64, num_stages=1, swizzle=16) also passed, compiled, and simulated at 402.23 us with 32768 smem; proxy cost dropped to 5.89 versus 10.93. Both attempts used num_stages=1 because the 32768-byte cap excludes large-tile multi-stage options, so pipeline depth has not yet been meaningfully explored. Domains are kept full (block_M/block_N/block_K/num_stages/swizzle all as allowed) to let HiGHS trade smaller tiles for extra stages within the cap and to keep testing swizzle>0 versus swizzle=0 at matched tile shapes. Swizzle is retained across [0,4,8,16] because the swizzle=16 run produced the lower simulated latency, though the reuse term is still an analytical hypothesis; we will again inspect simulator traffic/latency next round before trusting panel locality. Weights are adjusted modestly: pipeline raised to 1.5 since stage count has so far been pinned to 1 and deeper pipelining is a plausible lever once smaller tiles free smem; footprint lowered to 0.75 because actual smem sat at the cap in both runs, so footprint pressure is already enforced by the hard bound and does not need extra multiplicative weight. Traffic and launches stay at 1 for now to avoid overfitting on two points. The 32768-byte limit matches the hard portability cap and remains within [8192,49152]. Validation scope: Metal checks execute the exact source/config/TIR, but CUDA binaries are not executed on GB10; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements. No global optimality is claimed."}
